title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's 1986 'Analysis situs' draft, an attempt at a combinatorial, essentially 'pointless' foundation for stratified or tame spaces, in the spirit of 'topologie modérée' in Esquisse d'un programme §5. On the preceding pages he has a set Fé(d) of 'figures élémentaires' carrying three structures: a sub-object order ≤, a refinement relation ≪ (X' ≪ X means X' is a finer subdivision of X), and a compatibility relation. A 'figure' F is a set of compatible elementary figures, and he defines a combinatorial dimension as the sup of lengths of chains X_0 < … < X_{n-1} ≪ X_n.

On this page (his own numbering '17'; archive p.19) he moves to 'lieux' and to interpreting 'domaines' in terms of lieux.
(1) Terminology: he renames 'figures élémentaires' to 'multistrates', which he finds more telling. A natural reading is a union of strata that is order-convex ('o-convexe') in the closure poset of strata, i.e. a locally closed union of strata. So an arbitrary figure is a union of mutually compatible multistrates, closed under ≤ (saturated downward) and locally finite.
(2) Definition: a lieu is a multistrate that is minimal for ≪, i.e. it has no refinement other than itself. In the model examples (X a space, a multistrate being a family of parts of X), a minimal one is a family reduced to a single part that is a point. So lieux = points of X.
(3) He asserts that lieux are therefore also minimal for ≤. They are the o-convex multistrates admitting no refinement other than themselves.
(4) Let 𝓛 ⊂ M be the set of lieux, where M = Fé is the set of multistrates.

The next page carries out the purpose. To each multistrate X attach 𝓛_X, the set of lieux refining X, and the family 𝓛̂_X = {𝓛_Y : Y ≤ X}. He then tries to recover ≪ and compatibility on M from X ↦ 𝓛̂_X. This is a Stone-type representation: reconstructing an abstract lattice-like structure of 'regions' as sets of points, the points being defined intrinsically as minimal elements.
errors: The passage from 'minimal for ≪' to 'minimal for ≤' ('ce sont donc aussi…') is not justified. A proper sub-multistrate Y < X is not a priori a refinement of X, so an extra axiom linking ≤ and ≪ is needed.

Existence of enough minimal elements for ≪ is tacitly assumed. Without a descending-chain/atomicity hypothesis (e.g. semialgebraic sets over a non-archimedean real closed field, or o-minimal structures without enough definable points), minimal refinements need not exist or need not separate multistrates. The representation X ↦ 𝓛_X can then fail to be injective, and 'ideal points' (filters/types) would be needed instead of minimal elements.
Page numbering: Grothendieck's number '17' on archive page 19, following a page headed '18' (dated 11 June), suggests an inserted or reordered sheet. This is not a mathematical error.

ideas.what: Renaming elementary figures as 'multistrates': order-convex (locally closed) unions of strata as the basic building blocks of a combinatorial analysis situs
ideas.modern_name: locally closed unions of strata / constructible sets in a stratification; order-convex subsets of the stratification poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather); poset-of-strata viewpoint (MacPherson, Lurie's exit-path formalism)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 discusses tame topology and stratified structures, but not this terminology or axiomatics as far as I know

ideas.what: Points ('lieux') defined intrinsically as multistrates minimal for the refinement relation; domains to be reinterpreted as sets of lieux
ideas.modern_name: atoms / points of a lattice; Stone-type duality; points of a locale; types (ultrafilters) of a Boolean algebra of definable sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Stone (1936); Ehresmann/Isbell (locales); model theory (types); Coste–Roy (real spectrum)

ideas.what: Figures as locally finite, ≤-saturated unions of compatible multistrates
ideas.modern_name: locally finite stratified sets / constructible families

missed.claim: The page (with the next one) sets up a Stone-type reconstruction of a tame/stratified 'space' from a purely combinatorial structure (≤, ≪, compatibility), with points defined as ≪-minimal elements. Grothendieck works only with minimal elements, i.e. actual points. The natural completion is points as filters or types, which is exactly what the real spectrum (Coste–Roy) and o-minimal type spaces / Hrushovski–Loeser-style spaces do. The draft therefore anticipates a 'pointless' axiomatic tame topology whose point-recovery problem is the same as that solved by spectral spaces and type spaces. That link is not made in his texts and only partially in the later literature.
missed.quote: On appelle lieux … les multistrates qui sont minimales pour ≪, i.e. qui n'ont d'autres raffinements qu'elles-mêmes … Soit 𝓛 l'ensemble des lieux
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a possible axiomatic route to tame topology independent of a base field or o-minimal structure. It is of modest interest to people comparing o-minimality, real spectra and Grothendieck's 'topologie modérée' programme.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an interesting glimpse of Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatics for analysis situs, with the coinage 'multistrate' and points defined as refinement-minimal elements. But on this page the mathematics is definitional and close to standard lattice/Stone-duality ideas, and the hard step (reconstruction on the next page) is left unfinished.
transcription_corrections: Line 4 likely begins 'Mais en y repensant(?), au lieu des "figures élémentaires"…' rather than 'Mais au lieu de [?] ce que j'ai'.
'formant pour ≤' is probably 'fermée pour ≤' (i.e. saturated for ≤), followed by 'et loc. finie'.
'lieux de la catégorie[?]' may read 'lieux du contexte' (uncertain); the struck word before 'lieux' is 'multi-'.
'(des "[?]"' appears to be '(des "variétés"…' with the following line struck out.
'les non-[?] o-convexes' is uncertain; possibly 'mono-variétés' or similar.
'Fce' is probably 'Fé' (set of figures élémentaires = multistrates); the struck line before 'L ⊂ M' is 'Pour un…', replaced by 'donc'.
The page number written at top is '17' (Grothendieck's numbering), not matching archive page 19.
